Hormuz transit backfill: Kpler put Aug 13 at 13 crossings (+44% day on day) while Windward separately put Aug 14 at 13 (4 inbound, 9 outbound) but its own Aug 13 count was 3, a sharp cross-provider disagreement. President Trump vowed to declare the Strait of Hormuz 'a territory of the United States'; Iran's Gharibabadi said the strait stays blockaded until the US accepts 'the reality of defeat,' judiciary head Mohseni-Ejei called Iran 'the owner and ruler' of the strait. The June 17 MOU's 60-day toll-free Hormuz window lapses without a toll schedule or an extension announced; a third ADNOC vessel was struck transiting Hormuz late Friday. Yemen's government logged 181 operations against Houthi positions across Taiz, Marib, Abyan, Al-Dhalea and Al-Hudaydah in 24 hours, confirming IND-20260814-3 (spread beyond the original three fronts); fresh Houthi strikes hit Marib and al-Makha overnight. Saudi Arabia's continued restraint from direct retaliation for three Jazan refinery strikes falsifies IND-20260810-3 at its own deadline. Israel named a second Hezbollah Radwan commander killed in the Ansar strike and vowed further action; Hezbollah's promised response stayed rhetorical; Aoun, Salam and Berri condemned the strikes and a US State Department statement bluntly blamed Hezbollah. Jared Kushner met Egypt's Sisi and, via intermediaries, Hamas's Khalil al-Hayya in El Alamein, ahead of a Monday Netanyahu meeting; the IDF struck Islamic Jihad and Hamas operatives in Khan Yunis and Nuseirat following the Yellow Line incidents. In Qusra, ~15 re-entering settlers were turned away by the IDF but not arrested, and residents remain barred from some homes; Pope Leo XIV called for an end to West Bank violence, citing Qusra. New reporting that an August 11 settler attack breached the Taybeh closure falsifies IND-20260811-3.

Monday - Korean markets closed for the Liberation Day substitute holiday, so no new kospi/usdkrw observations; Friday's 6977.94/1418.3 carry forward. Brent settled -0.24% to 88.31 and WTI -0.8% to 81.74, holding most of last week's gains. President Trump told Fox News he would 'bomb the s*** out of' Oman 'if it gets in the way' of Hormuz talks, an unprecedented threat against a US partner, the same day the June 17 MOU's 60-day window expired unresolved; Iran's Baghaei claimed only an unfinished 'understanding' with Oman on the shipping map, still short of a joint statement, so IND-20260811-1 (no jointly confirmed mechanism, no Khamenei approval by its 08-18 deadline) resolves Confirmed. Kushner and Netanyahu agreed in a three-hour Jerusalem meeting that a US general should oversee Hamas's disarmament before any IDF redeployment, forming two working groups but taking no Security Cabinet vote; Hamas conditions disarmament on Israeli withdrawal and statehood recognition. Israel is reportedly ready to seize the Ali al-Taher ridge, Hezbollah's underground command hub in south Lebanon, pending a US green light. In the West Bank, soldiers dismantled some settler structures near besieged Qusra homes without broadly enforcing the closure order; Katz ordered a two-week plan to transfer enforcement to police; new settler outposts rose at Umm Safa and Burqa near Ramallah. Houthi spokesman Saree claimed a direct missile strike on a Saudi naval landing ship and escorts near Mocha plus a drone strike on a Marib arms depot, unconfirmed by Riyadh but potentially the war's most direct hit yet on Saudi military assets. Kpler put Hormuz transits at 3 for Aug 16, extending the sub-20/day regime.

Brent settled +$0.81 to 91.12 and WTI +$0.61 to 85.11 Tuesday, both a third straight gain and the highest since late July, after a projectile killed the chief engineer of the bulk carrier Minoan Dignity transiting outbound through Hormuz and Trump posted a map declaring the strait 'new U.S. territory' while saying there were 'no talks or conversations going on, or scheduled' with Iran and claiming the strait is 'open and operating.' Iran's parliament speaker Ghalibaf said the strait stays shut until US MOU commitments are met, and a senior Iranian official told Reuters Tehran is prepared to launch 'timely and precise strikes' to break the blockade; the Washington Post reported Trump's Oman bomb threat was driven by US opposition to joint Iran-Oman management of the strait's exit route, and Sen. Kaine's war powers resolution on Oman is now guaranteed a privileged Senate floor vote in September. The IAEA's Grossi gained Syria's first Deir Ezzor access in nearly 20 years and found 'tons' of undeclared nuclear material tied to the Assad-era Al Kibar program. In Qusra, Palestinian-American landlord Loui Ridi returned from Ohio and confronted the settlers occupying his home on its 10th day of siege; separately Katz's West Bank police handover plan was revealed to have been announced without IDF coordination, facing possible US, legal and electoral obstacles. KOSPI fell 1.55% to 6869.83, snapping a five-session winning streak, as 30-year Treasury yields hit their highest since 2007 and institutions sold Samsung Electronics; won firmed marginally to 1412.1. Kushner floated a 30-to-90-day Gaza disarmament timeline Hamas has not accepted.

Brent settled +0.7% to 91.62 and WTI +1.1% to 85.83, both a fourth straight gain and the highest since July 24, after the UAE's air defenses detected two ballistic missiles fired from Iran toward its waters targeting maritime navigation and ordered an immediate, indefinite halt to all trade and financial transactions with Iran; Iran's Baghaei rejected the claim as "baseless" and suggested a "false flag operation." Iran's IRGC reportedly detained a UAE-linked tanker off Qeshm Island for bypassing its designated route and fees, while two Chinese-crewed supertankers (Sea V, Hestia) and a separate UAE fuel tanker (Amara) reversed course mid-strait, continuing to contradict Trump's "open and operating" claim. KOSPI crashed 5.8% to 6471.17, the year's 48th circuit breaker, as offshore investors sold 3.48 trillion won and the 30-year US Treasury yield hit a 19-year high above 5.33%; the won nonetheless firmed to 1398.27, below 1400 for the first time since early October, on broad dollar weakness. The State Department notified Congress of $206 million in funding for Gaza's International Stabilization Force even as Israel and Hamas withhold acceptance of disarmament terms. The Qusra siege reached an 11th day with UN aid reaching the families but settlers still unenforced against; Katz's two-week IDF handover-plan deadline (~Aug 28) nears without a reported submission. IND-20260810-1 falsified at its ~08-20 deadline: no jointly announced, US-accepted Iran-Oman Hormuz mechanism materialized.

Brent settle +1.67% to 93.15 and WTI +2.16% to 86.21 Thursday, fifth straight gain, as Treasury Secretary Bessent vowed to 'collapse' Iran's regime via the toughest sanctions in history (rollout set Aug 24, dubbed 'ECONOMIC D-DAY' by Trump) and the UAE's Tuesday missile claim against Iran stayed without independent US/CENTCOM corroboration (CNBC; Bloomberg; Al Jazeera). KOSPI surged 5.89% to 6852.58, a near complete reversal of Wednesday's crash, on SK Hynix's 40 trillion won buyback and falling Treasury yields; year's 49th circuit breaker, first buy-side trigger of the stretch; won firmed further to 1392.6, an 11-month high (Korea Times; Seoul Economic Daily). IND-20260810-2 (Caine off-ramp) falsified at its 08-20 deadline: no public shift toward negotiation, continued escalatory rhetoric instead. Kushner and Mladenov's Israel visit closed out IND-20260814-2 falsified at its 08-21 deadline: Netanyahu called 15-point progress 'politically problematic' before the Oct 27 election and reiterated no pullback until full disarmament, restating rather than shifting his position despite Monday's working-groups agreement. Qusra's siege reached a twelfth day with trapped families reporting they have run out of food, Israeli forces still not enforcing the closure order against settlers. Yemen's government logged 100+ operations against Houthi positions in 24 hours as Houthi missiles struck Marib displacement camps, the UN citing the war's highest civil-war risk since the 2022 truce. Hormuz: Reuters via Kpler logged 6 vessels Wednesday Aug 19 against a 10-day average of 11, with Tuesday Aug 18 revised up to 9 from the 6 previously reported; no fresh Aug 20 print in the window.

Brent settle +0.84% to 93.93 and WTI +0.50% to 86.64 Friday, sixth straight gain and fresh one-month highs, as two Iran-pressure indicators tracked since July and mid-August both hit their own ~Aug 22 deadline: IND-20260723-1 (Congress appropriations) falsified after the Senate blocked debate on the defense bill carrying the war supplemental 50-46 in mid-July with no vote since, and IND-20260815-1 (Bessent's promised package) falsified as it slipped to a Monday Aug 24 press conference (Al Jazeera; PBS; CNN). KOSPI +0.88% to 6912.95, a second straight gain, on continued SK Hynix/Samsung buyback optimism; Kosdaq -4.63%; won firmed further to 1386.5, an 11-month high, touching 1380.3 intraday (Korea JoongAng Daily; Seoul Economic Daily). Yemen's war widened onto two fronts: Houthis claimed drone strikes on Saudi Arabia's Najran airport and Aramco facilities (unconfirmed by Riyadh), while Somali pirates hijacked the sanctioned Iran shadow-fleet tanker Sibu 1 off Mukalla, the second Gulf of Aden hijacking in four days (new IND-20260822-1, IND-20260822-2). The UK, Australia, Canada and Poland called Israel's closure of its World Central Kitchen strike investigation 'shameful'; separately Turkey, Egypt and Qatar condemned Israeli Gaza strikes that killed 16+ Palestinians since Tuesday as undermining the ceasefire. In Qusra, the IDF removed the besieging settlers and stationed soldiers at the homes' entrances, but residents say they remain barred from leaving under the same closure order. No fresh Hormuz Kpler print in the window; last verified count Wed Aug 19 (6).

Saturday - no settled markets, so no new brent/wti/kospi/usdkrw observations for 08-22 itself. Last verified levels remain Friday 08-21: Brent 93.93, WTI 86.64, KOSPI 6912.95, won 1386.5. Hormuz backfill: Reuters via Kpler put Thursday Aug 20 at 7 vessels (historic low per IranWire), half this same report's Aug 19 figure of 14, directly conflicting with the 6 already logged for Aug 19 elsewhere -- another instance of the series' recurring cross-report noise. Iran's Foreign Ministry called the sanctions package due at Monday's Bessent press conference a 'declaration of war on all nations' asserting unlawful 'extraterritorial sovereignty,' and warned any country joining the measures would be 'considered an enemy'; Trump repeated he views the Strait of Hormuz 'as an American territory right now' and said Iran is 'not ready to make the right deal' (Al Jazeera liveblog; CNBC). Separately Iran granted passage to a number of Iraqi oil tankers through Hormuz after repeated requests from Baghdad during parliament speaker Ghalibaf's Iraq visit, per Iraqi President Nizar Amedi -- the war's first concrete Hormuz passage concession to a third country (BOE Report; Al Jazeera; The National). Yemen's war intensified again: Marib's government media office said 6 ballistic missiles and 4 drones hit residential neighborhoods Saturday evening, wounding 4; Yemen's government logged 100-plus operations against Houthi positions in 24 hours, and 3 Houthi fighters including field commanders were killed in government drone strikes west of Taiz (New Arab; Al Jazeera). US special envoy Tom Barrack said Israel's Aug 18 strike on Syria's Abu al-Duhur airbase risked a direct military clash with Turkey, since Turkish forces were not told in advance and could have scrambled jets in response, and suggested in fresh remarks the strike may have been timed to 'bait' Ankara ahead of Israel's Oct 27 election; FM Sa'ar said Israel has 'no interest in escalation with Turkey' but will not accept a Turkish base in Syria (Haaretz; Times of Israel; JPost). IDF brass privately warned political leadership the West Bank is on the 'brink' of violent escalation over settler violence and outpost growth, as 4 more Palestinians were injured in separate settler attacks (a 15-year-old wounded near Tammun, a vehicle crash after stone-throwing near Ramallah) and the IDF killed a Hamas Deir al-Balah company commander, Sharif al-Hasanat, in central Gaza (Times of Israel liveblog).

Sunday - no settled markets, so no new brent/wti/kospi/usdkrw observations for 08-23 itself. Last verified levels remain Friday 08-21: Brent 93.93, WTI 86.64, KOSPI 6912.95, won 1386.5. No fresh Hormuz Kpler/Reuters print in the window; last verified Thursday 08-20 (7 vessels). Iran's new SNSC secretary Mohsen Rezaei threatened to halt all Hormuz oil flow if Gulf neighbors join Monday's US sanctions, while President Pezeshkian defended the collapsed June MOU, saying Iran 'cannot continue with war forever,' and Egypt's FM Abdelatty and Iran's Araghchi discussed reviving US-Iran talks (Middle East Eye; CNN; IRNA via The News, New Arab; Arab News). US envoy Tom Barrack, already central to the Turkey-Israel friction tracked Saturday, walked back a separate remark that Israel 'still' occupies the Golan Heights, contradicting Trump's 2019 recognition; Katz called the original remarks 'full of inaccuracies' and Sen. Rick Scott said Barrack 'forgot' Trump's position (Baltimore Sun; Times of Israel). Netanyahu and Katz warned of intensified strikes over Gaza kite launches (four found, no explosives) as separate strikes killed three Palestinians including 4-year-old Muhammad Abdel Salam Taha in Al-Zawayda and Nuseirat; ICRC facilitated release of six Palestinian detainees to Nasser Hospital (Times of Israel; Ahram Online; Arab News). A 24-year-old Israeli was stabbed in the Jordan Valley; settlers torched a car and room in Osarin near Nablus; army arrested 13 Palestinians; the EU urged Israel withdraw its E1 settlement tender (Times of Israel; Middle East Monitor). Yemeni army repelled a Houthi infiltration attempt on Taiz's Al-Dhabab front amid mutual shelling, following Saturday's Marib barrage (Yemen Monitor). Two indicators resolved Falsified at their own ~08-24 deadline: IND-20260724-1 (Saudi Abraham Accords linkage, no movement in a month) and IND-20260814-1 (Hormuz toll question, no formal toll schedule or blanket extension, only the narrower Iraqi carve-out).
